h1: A whole-home remodel changes everything but the address
hero_sub: Full-gut renovations, layout changes and structural openings for high-end homes from Coral Gables to the Broward waterfront. Every project permitted, inspected and supervised daily, under Florida general contractor license CGC1539072.
intro_paragraphs: A whole-home remodel at this level is not a refresh. It is a house taken back to its structure and rebuilt inside its own walls: partitions removed, ceilings opened, mechanical systems replaced end to end, every opening reglazed, and a floor plan redrawn around how the family actually lives. The owners who commission this work are rarely first-time renovators. They love the street, the lot or the water view, and they have decided that the shortest path to the house they want runs through the one already standing rather than through demolition and three years of ground-up construction.

Miami-Dade and Broward together form the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, and the code here follows the weather. Windows, doors, roofing and shutters carry Miami-Dade Notices of Acceptance, and a statewide Florida Product Approval counts inside the zone only if it was evaluated for the HVHZ. Close to the ocean the code also gets specific about corrosion resistance in fasteners and connectors, and chlorides work steadily into concrete until reinforcing steel rusts and pushes the surface off. Then there is water from below. In a flood zone, a remodel that reaches half the building's value stops being a remodel and becomes a compliance project.

There is no single permit office for this market. Miami-Dade has thirty-four municipalities and Broward thirty-one, each running its own building department, with the counties permitting the unincorporated areas. Each county layers its own amendments over the Florida Building Code through a Board of Rules and Appeals, the body that certifies the inspectors you will eventually meet, and Miami-Dade's Product Control section writes the approvals both counties rely on. Add a condominium board or an architectural review committee and three approvals sit in a row. We price against a fixed written scope before demolition, sequence the job around those reviews, keep a supervisor on site every working day, pass the inspections in order, and close the permit at the end.

The range is the point. We remodel Merrick-era Mediterraneans in Coral Gables, postwar houses in Miami Shores and Ponce-Davis, oceanfront apartments in Bal Harbour and Sunny Isles Beach, and prewar houses on the Venetian Islands and in Coconut Grove. North of the county line the work turns to the Fort Lauderdale waterfront, through Las Olas Isles, Harbor Beach, Rio Vista and Coral Ridge, then Lighthouse Point, Hillsboro Beach and Hollywood Lakes, and finally the western estate areas of Parkland, Southwest Ranches, Plantation Acres and Weston. Forty-two areas, each with its own page here, its own building department, and its own list of things that go wrong.
scope_heading: What a whole-home remodel actually covers
scope_intro: Every house is different, but a full gut in this market is assembled from the same six pieces. All six get priced and written down before anyone swings a hammer.

scope_items.name: Structure and layout changes
scope_items.desc: Removing bearing walls, widening openings and setting steel or engineered beams, with calculations signed and sealed by an engineer and carried intact through plan review.

scope_items.name: Electrical, plumbing and HVAC
scope_items.desc: New service and panel, a full rewire, supply and drain lines replaced, and a right-sized air conditioning design with duct runs drawn for the house you are about to have.

scope_items.name: Impact windows and doors
scope_items.desc: Glazing and entry systems carrying Miami-Dade Notices of Acceptance for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, detailed at the opening so the wall behind them stays dry.

scope_items.name: Envelope and coastal detailing
scope_items.desc: Roof, stucco, waterproofing and corrosion-resistant fasteners and connectors where the code requires them near saltwater, plus concrete repair when spalling turns up behind a finish.

scope_items.name: Kitchens, baths and millwork
scope_items.desc: Both wet trades folded into the larger job, so plumbing, waterproofing, stone and cabinetry are sequenced once rather than repeated later under a permit of their own.

scope_items.name: Approvals, inspections and closeout
scope_items.desc: Association and design-review packages, permit applications, inspection scheduling and the final certificate, so the permit closes properly instead of aging open on your property record.

faqs.q: What does a whole-home remodel cost in Miami-Dade or Broward?
faqs.a: There is no honest single number, and anyone who gives you one over the phone is quoting a different house. A cosmetic refresh, a full gut with new mechanicals, and a gut that also moves structure and reglazes every opening are three different projects with three different budgets. What we commit to is a written scope with the products named and the allowances tied to real selections, so the number you sign is the number you pay unless something genuinely unforeseen appears and gets documented. We are not the cheap bid, and we say so early.

faqs.q: How long does a full-gut remodel take?
faqs.a: Think in three blocks: design and engineering, approvals, then construction. Drawings and structural calculations for a whole house generally take a couple of months. Approvals depend on your municipality and on whether an association or a design review board sees the plans first. Construction on a full house commonly runs several months to a year, and custom cabinetry, stone and imported glazing stretch the tail. You get a written schedule alongside the estimate, and daily supervision whose entire job is defending it.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remodel my whole house?
faqs.a: Yes. Structural work, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, windows, doors and roofing all require permits in both counties, and unpermitted work surfaces later at the worst possible moment, usually during a sale. Florida law puts outside limits on how long a municipality can hold a complete residential application, but the clock does not start until the submittal is genuinely complete. That is where the delays actually live, and it is why we assemble drawings, engineering and product data before filing rather than after the first round of comments.

faqs.q: What derails a remodel after demolition?
faqs.a: Rarely the construction itself. Jobs stall on correction cycles from plan review, approvals written for a product nobody actually ordered, association packages filed out of order, and discovery: unpermitted work by a previous owner, an undersized electrical service, rotten sheathing, or concrete spalling hiding behind a finish on a coastal house. Long-lead glazing and cabinetry can idle a crew for weeks. We front-load the surprises by opening exploratory areas early and writing whatever we find into the scope.

faqs.q: Who runs the job while we are living somewhere else?
faqs.a: A PGX supervisor, every working day, on your job. Subcontractors work to our permit and our schedule rather than their own. PGX Builders Group is a licensed and insured Florida general contractor, Lic. CGC1539072, twenty-plus years of it here, with more than 150 remodels and additions completed in this market, each of them permitted and inspected. The same people stay with the job from first estimate to warranty call, so there is one number to dial and one person accountable for the answer.

faqs.q: Does the FEMA 50 percent rule apply to my remodel?
faqs.a: It applies if the home sits in a Special Flood Hazard Area and the cost of the improvement equals or exceeds fifty percent of the building's pre-improvement market value. Cross that line and the whole structure has to be brought into compliance with current floodplain rules, which generally means elevating the lowest floor to base flood elevation plus freeboard. Some cities count permit values cumulatively over a set period rather than job by job. We check the flood zone and the arithmetic before anyone draws anything.
